study.question: Classify every decision the orchestrator seat has actually made across its lifetime into (a) mechanized, (b) lookup, (c) judgment. S04 phase 0.

denominator.primary_definition: DISTINCT seat decisions. One row per decision; a decision broadcast to N lanes, or executed against N rows, is ONE row with events=N. Includes decisions issued by sprint-console/delegator seats (kind=console), which held the same routing authority.
denominator.events_definition: Decision EVENTS — the same population counted once per lane/row touched. Use this denominator for 'how often did the seat have to act', the primary for 'how many distinct calls did it have to make'.

excluded.why: probe = tell/inbox self-tests and one empty record, no decision content; inbound = worker->seat messages (the seat's answer is a decision but the RECORD is the worker's, so they are counted separately as escalations RECEIVED: 4); peer = worker->worker coordination with no seat in the loop.

source_totals.docs/infra/managent/directives.jsonl: 105 records parsed (the file is 191 lines because notes embed newlines; 105 objects, IDs are NOT unique - the counter reset on 2026-08-19, so D021-D054 each appear twice with different targets and timestamps). 88 seat/console decisions, 9 probes, 4 inbound, 4 peer.
source_totals.docs/infra/managent/archive.json: 104 archived rows; 31 carry a seat close/retire/adjudicate decision (20 test-leakage phantom closes + T203 foreclosure + 8 epitaphs + 3 verdict adjudications), collapsing to 8 distinct decisions + 1 excluded probe epitaph (TL1A).
source_totals.docs/status/ROADMAP-2026-08-20.md: 8 numbered rulings in the rev-3 ruling queue (:207-:278).
source_totals.findings/T568-orcha-successor-seat.json: 6 enumerated decisions in the notes field.

denominator.extraction_rule: Directives and archive rows are enumerated exhaustively (every record classified, none skipped). Prose handover docs are mined ONLY for numbered/enumerated decision items, so the count is re-derivable by anyone opening the same lines; unnumbered narrative in those docs is deliberately not counted, which makes the (c) column a LOWER bound and the mechanized fraction correspondingly an upper bound.
denominator.not_counted: orchestration-layer-spec.md §7/§7b rulings 1-10 are OPERATOR rulings recorded by the seat, not seat decisions. ROADMAP-2026-08-21 §'Ruling queue - open' items 1-4 are escalations still open, i.e. decisions NOT made.

mechanized_breakdown.definition: mechanism_class on every (a) row names WHICH existing mechanism already covers it (counts over seat rows).

lookup_breakdown.definition: table on every (b) row names WHICH data table decides it (counts over seat rows).

judgment_subsplit.definition: Every (c) row carries a c_kind. relay = operator-originated content the seat carried or interpreted; doctrine = a rule/policy the seat authored; scope = re-specifying a live row's brief mid-flight; verdict = evaluating a worker's or an instrument's result; triage = escalation / stall / ownership / novel-situation routing.

reconciler_scope.basis: S04 seed §9 scopes the reconciler to STEADY STATE only - routing, health, closure, escalation - and explicitly leaves sprint decomposition, spec authorship, grand audits and direction to the operator-and-strong-agent conversation. relay/doctrine/scope are exactly that conversation.

findings.statement: Column (c) is 56 of 129 distinct seat decisions (43.4%), but only 25 of 129 (19.4%) fall inside the reconciler's own scope boundary. The other 31 are operator relay (15), doctrine authorship (10) and mid-flight re-scoping (6) - all three are S04 seed §9 non-goals.
findings.consequence: The sprint shrinks. The reconciler's verb set has to cover verdict evaluation (15) and triage (10), not 43% of the seat's history. The seed's own bet - 'if the table shows (c) is small, the sprint shrinks accordingly' - resolves to a scope of roughly one fifth of the record.

findings.statement: Mechanized (a) is 61 distinct rows but 84 decision EVENTS - 55.3% of all events against 47.3% of distinct decisions. The gap is broadcast: the seat repeated one mechanical decision to 2-3 lanes at a time (DIR-022..024 suite stop, DIR-025..027 resume, DIR-028..030 kill, DIR-065..068 the git-add-A sweep and its follow-up).
findings.consequence: A queue-level condition reaches every lane at once. The per-lane repetition is pure seat tax and disappears with the mechanism, which is why the events denominator matters as much as the distinct one.

findings.statement: Column (b) is only 12 of 129 (9.3%), and it is dominated by ONE table: provider quota / appetite, 7 of 12 (Ollama cooldown DIR-073, token cost DIR-075, wind-downs DIR-079/080, weekly exhaustion DIR-087, the Claude 15:30 reset DIR-089, the reset-driven reorder DIR-092). The remainder is model-fit 2, ordering 2, measurement-validity 1.
findings.consequence: Absorbing column (b) needs a provider/appetite table first and an ordering table second - both already named in orchestration-layer-spec §3 (conditions) and §7 rulings 1-2. No new design is owed for (b); it is data entry.

findings.statement: The largest mechanized family is the one-writer class: 12 of the 61 (a) seat rows, plus 3 more recorded as worker-to-worker peer coordination (15 records in total), plus 2 registration rows (holds declared at mint). `managent claim` has refused on holds conflict for the whole period (src/managent/main.zig:2059 and :2121) - so every one of those 15 records is a conflict the mechanism was already able to prevent and did not, because holds= was never registered. DIR-098 is the sharpest case: the SEAT ITSELF dispatched T545 onto src/managent/main.zig without declaring holds, then had to pause T544 by hand.
findings.consequence: The recurring failure is registration, not enforcement. T568's own closing lesson says the same thing independently (`suggest` mints the row before the bundle header exists, so holds= never records; register bundle-FIRST via `managent add --bundle --holds`). Making holds= mandatory at mint is the single highest-yield fix this table exposes, and it is cheaper than anything in the reconciler design.

findings.statement: 9 of the 105 directive records carry no decision at all (eight tell/inbox self-test probes and one record with no note field), and 4 more are worker-to-worker peer coordination in which the seat never appears.
findings.consequence: Any metric computed over raw directives.jsonl without this partition overstates seat activity by ~12%. It also means the directive log is already doing double duty as an instrument-test channel, which the reconciler's run records should keep separate.

findings.statement: The seat corrected or superseded its OWN prior directive 6 times (DIR-035 over D038, DIR-041 over D048, DIR-101 over D049, DIR-050 over D056, DIR-096 retracting its own G1 instruction, DIR-105 over D053), and twice apologised for damage it caused itself (DIR-065..068, `git add -A` sweeping two lanes' work into the seat's commit; DIR-098, the missing holds above).
findings.consequence: A stateless per-wake reconciler cannot accumulate this particular debt - it has no prior directive of its own to defend - but the escalation contract must explicitly permit one wake to retract a previous wake's action through the store, or the same correction will simply become an escalation.

findings.statement: Escalations RECEIVED by the seat number only 4 across the entire record (worker->ORCHA directives: DIR-072, DIR-083, DIR-084, DIR-095). Two are genuine blocks and both have the identical shape - a gate fired correctly (the done gate on a dirty tracked deliverable; the pre-commit C7 gate on another console's non-conforming findings file) and the unblock needed a cross-lane routing decision. The other two are status reports that the store already contained.
findings.consequence: The inbound half of the escalation contract is tiny and has one dominant pattern: gate-fired-correctly-but-blocked-on-another-lane. It has already recurred, so by S04 §6's corollary it owes a rule, not a reconciler judgment - route the blocking file to its owning row. The two status-report records argue for the contract forbidding 'report' as an escalation category at all, since `managent done` already records it.

findings.statement: Not one decision in the record was classified (a) on the strength of a tool that could exist; every (a) row names a mechanism verified present at HEAD (2b03b6b-dirty). The three (a) rows whose mechanism is 'message-transport' (DIR-067, DIR-068, DIR-101) are a different kind, though: they exist only because a directive's own text was mangled by shell quoting or a failed interpolation.
findings.consequence: The reconciler must emit directives through a template, not through a shell string. Three of the seat's decisions were spent repairing its own message formatting.
